Ravindra: Ran nightly perf job for canary-stable with the new FlashAttention kernel + paged-KV warmup. Seeing a sharp p99 regression on small-seq (<=64) conversational workload. p50 roughly same, but p95/p99 up ~20-35%.

Ravindra: Quick summary: batch formation collapsed to a lot more tiny batches (1-2 requests) after the kernel switch. Suspect interaction between kernel latency tail and token-budget slotting.

Ravindra: Snippet from profiler (aggregated across 10k requests):
```
workload: small-seq chat
avg_batch_size: 1.9 (was 7.8 baseline)
kv_warmup_ms: 0.8 -> 4.6
flash_kernel_latency_ms (attn): 0.5 -> 0.9 (median)
queue_wait_ms: +12ms p95
```

Sophie: ugh. do we have flamegraphs or a request timeline? is the batcher pre-slotting or post-slotting? :thinking:

Ravindra: attaching timeline in the perf job logs (link) and a condensed request trace: each incoming req triggers paged-KV zeroing/warmup in the kernel path which adds jitter. Batcher slotting currently uses token_budget_target=64 + slot_hysteresis=0.15 so when a request hits the longer kernel path it times out the rest and flushes early.

Andrew: If the kernel adds jitter at attention entry, the continuous batcher will see inconsistent completion times and will start emitting small batches. Two options: 1) increase token_budget_target or 2) change slotting to be latency-aware (hold for extra X ms when variance high).

Maria: Can we short-circuit paged-KV warmup for small-seq until batch is formed? i.e., defer paged-KV allocation to after batch formation or do a cheap check for seq_len <= 64?

Ravindra: tried a quick patch to defer paged-KV prefetch:
```diff
- warmup_paged_kv(req)
+ if (req.seq_len > 64 || req.flags.force_kv_warmup) warmup_paged_kv(req)
```
Ravindra: After that patch in local perf, avg_batch_size bumped to 5.6 and p99 dropped back ~12%. Not a complete fix but promising.

Sophie: nice. any regression against long-seq? we should only gate by small-seq. Also watch for downstream memory thrash if many long sequences land together.

Andrew: short-term mitigation: bump token_budget_target from 64 -> 128 and add a cheap jitter-based hold: if observed_kernel_jitter_ms > 2ms then hold_max_ms = 8. That should avoid premature flushes while we iterate on warmup.

Ravindra: scheduled a canary with the deferred-warmup patch + token_budget_target=128. ci-bot: canary-deploy queued for gpu-canary-03.

ci-bot: canary deployment started (job id: canary-2145001234-7). logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/2145001234-7

Maria: also flagging the FlashAttention commit (rev: f1a2b3) for rollback if canary fails. we should capture kernel-level histograms too (per-layer attn latency) to see if a specific operator changed.

Sophie: agree. add per-kernel histos to the perf job and a small-heap memory tracker to ensure the defer doesn't spike memory.

Andrew: if canary shows improvement, we should still schedule an A/B to test under load with mixed seq distribution. quick patch LGTM otherwise.

Ravindra: thanks all — will post canary result here once CI finishes. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: canary job completed: succeeded on basic smoke (no crash), perf-run still running (~6m remaining).

Ravindra: perf-run finished: avg_batch_size=6.1, p99 down 15% vs kernel-only canary, memory delta +3% under peak. scheduling a longer soak to validate.

Maria: good. create a follow-up issue to add slotting telemetry (score per-slot, observed variance) and a test that simulates kernel-level jitter to prevent regressions.

Sophie: noted. I'll add the telemetry checklist to the perf-playbook.

Andrew: TL;DR: kernel jitter from FlashAttention + eager paged-KV warmup caused continuous batcher to emit tiny batches. Mitigation: defer warmup for small sequences + increase token_budget_target and introduce jitter-aware hold. Follow-ups: per-kernel histos, A/B soak, revert gate if needed.

Ravindra: filing the issue now and assigning to eng-runtime. issue: https://tracker.internal/RED-3581

Maria: ack. :white_check_mark:

Sophie: thanks everyone.
